admin_units.State_Name: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu

temples.name: Sri Venkateswara Swamy Temple
alternativeNames: Tirumala Balaji Temple; Tirupati Temple; Seven Hills Temple; Srivari Temple
temples.description: Perched atop the sacred Venkatadri hill of the Seshachalam range, Sri Venkateswara Temple is one of the world's most revered pilgrimage destinations. The self-manifested (Swayambhu) deity stands majestically under the gilded Ananda Nilayam vimana.
deities: Vakuladevi, Yoga Narasimha, Varadaraja, Garuda, Ramanuja, Vishwaksena
temples.templeType: Ancient Hill Temple Complex / Divya Desam
temples.establishedYear: Pallava, Chola, Pandya, and Vijayanagara dynastic additions (9th-16th c. CE)
temples.address: S V Temple, Tirumala, Tirupati, Andhra Pradesh
temples.ticketRequired: Optional (Free Sarva Darshan available; Paid SED ₹300)
temples.majorFestivals: Srivari Annual Salakatla Brahmotsavam, Vaikunta Ekadasi, Rathasapthami, Ugadi Asthanam

temples.name: Sri Padmavathi Ammavari Temple
temples.description: The holy abode of Goddess Padmavathi, consort of Lord Venkateswara, seated on a golden lotus. Pilgrimage tradition holds that visiting Tirumala is fulfilled only after worshipping Devi Padmavathi at Tiruchanur.
deities: Sri Krishna, Balarama, Sundararaja Swamy, Surya Narayana Swamy
temples.address: Tiruchanur Road, Tirupati, Andhra Pradesh
temples.majorFestivals: Karthika Brahmotsavam, Panchami Theertham, Vasantotsavam, Navaratri

temples.name: Sri Kalahasteeswara Temple
temples.description: One of the five sacred Pancha Bhoota Sthalas representing the element Air (Vayu). The flame inside the sanctum flickers continuously even though there are no air vents. Famous worldwide for Rahu-Ketu Sarpa Dosha Nivarana pujas.
deities: Goddess Gnana Prasunambika, Pathala Vinayaka, Kannappa
temples.templeType: Pancha Bhoota Sthalam (Vayu Lingam) / Paadal Petra Sthalam
temples.address: Srikalahasti, Tirupati District, Andhra Pradesh
temples.ticketRequired: Optional (Free Darshan queue; Paid Puja tickets)
temples.majorFestivals: Maha Shivaratri Brahmotsavam (13 days), Giri Pradakshina, Nandi Seva

temples.name: Sri Bhramaramba Mallikarjuna Swamy Temple
alternativeNames: Srisailam Temple; Srisailam Jyotirlinga & Shakti Peetham
temples.description: One of India's rarest sacred sites that is simultaneously a Jyotirlinga of Lord Shiva and a Maha Shakti Peetham of Goddess Parvati (Bhramaramba). Surrounded by the pristine Nallamala forests overlooking the Pathalaganga (Krishna River).
deities: Vriddha Mallikarjuna, Sahasra Linga, Vighneswara, Annapurna
temples.address: Srisailam, Nandyal District, Andhra Pradesh
temples.source: Sri Bhramaramba Mallikarjuna Swamy Devasthanam Gazette
temples.ticketRequired: Optional (Free Darshan available; ₹150 Special Entry; ₹500 Sparsha Darshan)
temples.majorFestivals: Maha Shivaratri Brahmotsavam (7 days), Ugadi Mahotsavam, Kumbhothsavam

temples.name: Sri Durga Malleswara Swamy Varla Devasthanam
temples.nameLocal: శ్రీ దుర్గా మల్లేశ్వర స్వామి వార్ల దేవస్థానం (కనకదుర్గ గుడి)
temples.description: Standing majestically atop Indrakeeladri hill on the banks of the Krishna River in Vijayawada. Goddess Kanaka Durga is self-manifested (Swayambhu) with eight arms bearing divine weapons, holding the demon Mahishasura in battle victory.
deities: Lord Malleswara Swamy, Subrahmanya Swamy, Nataraja
temples.address: Indrakeeladri, Vijayawada, NTR District, Andhra Pradesh
temples.source: Sri Durga Malleswara Swamy Varla Devasthanam
temples.majorFestivals: Dasara Navaratri (10 days), Shakambhari Utsavams, Bhavani Deeksha Viramana

temples.name: Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple
temples.nameLocal: శ్రీ లక్ష్మీ నరసింహ స్వామి దేవస్థానం యాదాద్రి
temples.description: One of India's most breathtaking modern architectural reconstructions, rebuilt completely using 250,000 tonnes of pure black granite (Krishna Shila) based on Kakatiya and Dravidian temple treatises without concrete, encasing the ancient sanctum cave.
temples.mainDeity: Lord Narasimha (Pancha Narasimha Kshetram: Jwala, Yogananda, Gandabherunda, Ugra, Lakshmi Narasimha)
deities: Goddess Lakshmi, Sri Rama, Anjaneya Swamy, Alwars
temples.templeType: Ancient Cave Shrine & Modern Monolithic Krishna Shila Temple Complex
temples.address: Yadagirigutta, Yadadri Bhuvanagiri District, Telangana
temples.source: Yadadri Temple Development Authority (YTDA) Official Gazette
temples.ticketRequired: Optional (Free Dharma Darshan; ₹150 Special Entry; ₹300 VIP)
temples.majorFestivals: Annual Brahmotsavam (11 days), Narasimha Jayanthi, Vaikunta Ekadasi, Rathotsavam

temples.name: Sri Sita Ramachandra Swamy Temple
temples.nameLocal: శ్రీ సీతారామచంద్ర స్వామి వారి దేవస్థానం భద్రాచలం
temples.description: Known as the Dakshina Ayodhya on the serene banks of sacred Godavari River. Lord Rama appears here uniquely in Vaikuntha Rama form with four arms holding Shankha, Chakra, Bow, and Arrow, with Sita Devi seated gracefully on his left lap.
temples.mainDeity: Lord Rama (Vaikuntha Rama with conch, discus, bow, and arrow) & Sita Devi
temples.address: Bhadrachalam, Bhadradri Kothagudem District, Telangana
temples.source: Sri Sita Ramachandra Swamy Devasthanam Register
temples.majorFestivals: Sri Rama Navami (Kalyanotsavam), Vaikunta Ekadasi (Teppotsavam on Godavari)

temples.name: Ramappa Temple (Rudreshwara Swamy)
alternativeNames: Ramalingeswara Temple Palampet; UNESCO World Heritage Site
temples.description: An inscription dates this Kakatiya marvel to 1213 CE, constructed under general Recharla Rudra. The only temple in India named after its master sculptor (Ramappa). Inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2021 for its floating bricks technology, sandbox earthquake foundations, and bracket dancer statues.
temples.templeType: UNESCO World Heritage Site / Monumental Stone Temple
temples.address: Palampet, Venkatapur Mandal, Mulugu District, Telangana
temples.ticketRequired: Yes (ASI entry ticket ₹25 for Indians, ₹300 foreigners; free for children under 15)
temples.majorFestivals: Maha Shivaratri (3-day fair), Ramappa Dance Festival (Kakatiya Heritage Festival)

temples.name: Arulmigu Meenakshi Sundareshwarar Temple
alternativeNames: Madurai Meenakshi Amman Temple; Thiruvalavayan Kovil
temples.description: One of the greatest architectural triumphs of Dravidian culture. The 14-acre temple complex is crowned by 14 monumental gopurams, the tallest being the Southern Tower rising 170 feet, encrusted with over 1,500 brightly colored stucco figures, surrounding the sacred Golden Lotus Pond (Potramarai Kulam).
deities: Mukkuruni Vinayagar, Subramanya, Ayiram Kaal Mandapam deities
temples.templeType: Monumental Dravidian Temple City / Paadal Petra Sthalam / Shakta Peetham
temples.establishedYear: 6th Century BCE origin; expanded 16th-17th Century CE by Nayakas
temples.address: Madurai Meenakshi Temple, Madurai, Tamil Nadu
temples.ticketRequired: Optional (Free General Darshan; ₹100 Special Entry; ₹50 Hall of 1000 Pillars)
temples.majorFestivals: Chithirai Thiruvizha (1 month festival), Meenakshi Tirukkalyanam, Navaratri, Avani Moola Utsavam

temples.name: Arulmigu Ramanathaswamy Temple
alternativeNames: Rameswaram Temple; Char Dham Rameswaram; 22 Theerthams Shrine
temples.description: One of the holy Char Dham sites and a Jyotirlinga. Celebrated for its third outer corridor (Chokkattan Mandapam) spanning 1,220 metres with 1,212 intricately carved monolithic sandstone pillars. Pilgrims take holy bath in 22 sacred Theerthams (wells) inside the temple.
temples.mainDeity: Lord Shiva (Ramanathaswamy - Sand Lingam consecrated by Sita Devi)
deities: Goddess Parvathavardhini, Viswanatha Lingam (brought by Hanuman), Setu Madhava
temples.templeType: Char Dham Pilgrimage Site / Jyotirlinga (7th) / Paadal Petra Sthalam
temples.address: Rameswaram, Ramanathapuram District, Tamil Nadu
temples.ticketRequired: Optional (Free Darshan; ₹25 Theertham Snanam; ₹100 Special Darshan)
temples.majorFestivals: Maha Shivaratri (10 days), Thirukalyanam (Aadi Amavasai), Ramalinga Prathishta Utsavam

temples.name: Arulmigu Brihadisvara Temple (Big Temple)
alternativeNames: Peruvudaiyar Kovil; Thanjavur Big Temple; Rajarajeswaram
temples.description: Consecrated in 1010 CE by Emperor Raja Raja Chola I. One of the greatest achievements of world architecture. The 216-foot vimana is crowned by an 80-tonne monolithic granite cupola. Constructed entirely of inter-locking granite without mortar in a region devoid of granite quarries.
deities: Periyanayaki Amman, Murugan, Ganesha, Nandi (monolithic 20-tonne bull)
temples.templeType: UNESCO World Heritage Site / Great Living Chola Temple
temples.establishedYear: 1003–1010 CE (Completed in the 25th regnal year of Raja Raja Chola I)
temples.address: Membalam Road, Balaganapathy Nagar, Thanjavur, Tamil Nadu
temples.ticketRequired: Free Entry (ASI Monument & HR&CE Active Temple)
temples.majorFestivals: Sathaya Vizha (Birth anniversary of Raja Raja Chola I), Maha Shivaratri, Chithirai Brahmotsavam

temples.name: Udupi Sri Krishna Matha
alternativeNames: Udupi Krishna Temple; Kanakana Kindi Temple; Ashta Mathas of Udupi
temples.description: Founded in the 13th century by Jagadguru Sri Madhvacharya. The deity is viewed uniquely through the silver-plated nine-holed window known as Navagraha Kindi and Kanakana Kindi. Administered cyclically by the Eight Mathas (Ashta Mathas) in the biennial Paryaya system.
temples.mainDeity: Lord Bala Krishna (Child Krishna holding churning rod)
temples.templeType: Historic Monastic Temple Complex / Dvaita Vedanta Epicentre
temples.address: Car Street, Udupi, Karnataka
temples.source: Sri Krishna Matha Paryaya Official Records
temples.ticketRequired: Free Entry (No ticket required for holy Kindi Darshan)
temples.majorFestivals: Biennial Paryaya Mahotsava (every 2 years in January), Sri Krishna Janmashtami, Vittal Pindi, Laksha Deepotsava

temples.name: Sri Murudeshwar Temple
alternativeNames: Murudeshwara Shiva Temple; World's 2nd Tallest Shiva Statue
temples.description: Perched on Kanduka Giri hill surrounded on three sides by the roaring waters of the Arabian Sea. Features the world's second tallest statue of Lord Shiva (123 feet) and a towering 20-story Raja Gopuram (249 feet) equipped with a high-speed elevator taking visitors to viewing galleries overlooking the sea.
temples.architecture: Dravidian with Modern Coastal Monumental Engineering
temples.establishedYear: Ancient origin; 20-story Gopuram and Colossal Statue completed 2002–2008 CE
temples.address: Murudeshwar, Bhatkal Taluk, Uttara Kannada, Karnataka
temples.ticketRequired: Free Entry for Temple; ₹20 for Raja Gopuram Lift to 18th floor
temples.majorFestivals: Maha Shivaratri (grand seaside mela and Rathotsava), Karthika Deepotsava

temples.name: Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple
temples.description: One of the 108 Divya Desams and the royal temple of the Travancore Royal Family. The 18-foot presiding deity of Lord Padmanabha reposes on the serpent Adi Shesha, sculpted using 12,008 sacred Saligrama stones brought from the Gandaki River in Nepal covered in Katusarkara yogam, viewed through three separate doors.
temples.mainDeity: Lord Padmanabha (Maha Vishnu in Ananthasayanam posture on five-hooded serpent Anantha)
temples.address: West Nada, East Fort, Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala
temples.source: Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple Official Administrative Register
temples.ticketRequired: Optional (Free General Queue; Paid Special Darshan passes ₹150, ₹250)
temples.majorFestivals: Alpasi Utsavam, Painkuni Utsavam, Aaraattu (procession to Shangumugham Beach), Lakshadeepam

temples.name: Guruvayur Sree Krishna Temple
temples.description: Known as Bhuloka Vaikuntham (Heaven on Earth). The sacred deity is made of Patala Anjanasila (black bismuth stone). Sanctified according to tradition by Guru (Brihaspati) and Vayu (Wind God) who installed the deity worshipped by Lord Krishna himself in Dwarka before it submerged.
temples.mainDeity: Lord Guruvayurappan (Unnikrishnan / Lord Vishnu with four arms holding Shankha, Chakra, Gada, Padma)
temples.templeType: Historic Mahakshetram / Premier Krishna Shrine of South India
temples.architecture: Kerala Pagoda Style with Copper Tiled Roofs
temples.establishedYear: Ancient traditional origin; rebuilt 1638 CE; golden flagstaff erected 1952
temples.address: Guruvayur, Thrissur District, Kerala
temples.source: Guruvayur Devaswom Managing Committee Official Register
temples.ticketRequired: Optional (Free General Queue; Senior Citizens Queue; Paid Special Pass ₹1000)
temples.majorFestivals: Guruvayur Utsavam (10 days with Elephant Race / Anayottam), Chembai Music Festival, Guruvayur Ekadasi

temples.name: Arulmigu Manakula Vinayagar Temple
alternativeNames: Manakula Vinayagar Temple; White Town Ganesha
temples.description: Predating French colonial rule in Puducherry by centuries. Situated in the charming French Quarter near the Promenade Beach. Celebrated for its golden vimana (plated with 7.5 kg of gold), 40 painted incarnations of Ganesha on the ceiling, and the beloved temple elephant Lakshmi.
temples.mainDeity: Lord Ganesha (Bhuvaneshar Ganapathy facing East towards the Bay of Bengal)
temples.establishedYear: Pre-1666 CE origin; golden vimana gilded 2003 CE
temples.address: Manakula Vinayagar Koil Street, White Town, Puducherry
temples.source: Government of Puducherry Hindu Religious Institutions Registry
temples.majorFestivals: Vinayaka Chaturthi (24-day festival), Brahmotsavam, Sankatahara Chaturthi

temples.name: Shri Kashi Vishwanath Temple
temples.nameLocal: श्री काशी विश्वनाथ ज्योतिर्लिंग मंदिर वाराणसी
alternativeNames: Golden Temple Varanasi; Vishweswara Temple; Kashi Dham
temples.description: Located on the western bank of holy Ganga in the eternal city of Varanasi. One of the twelve sacred Jyotirlingas, revered as the spiritual capital of Hinduism where Lord Shiva grants liberation (Moksha). The monumental Kashi Vishwanath Dham Corridor (expanded to 500,000 sq ft) connects the sanctum directly to the sacred Ganga ghats.
temples.mainDeity: Lord Shiva (Vishwanatha - Ruler of the Universe)
deities: Maa Annapurna, Dandapani, Avimukteshwara, Kaal Bhairav, Dhundhiraj Ganesha
temples.historicalPeriod: Late 18th Century CE to Modern Era
temples.establishedYear: Ancient origin; sanctum 1780 CE; golden spires 1835; Corridor 2021 CE
temples.address: Kashi Vishwanath Corridor, Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh
temples.source: Shri Kashi Vishwanath Temple Trust Gazette
temples.ticketRequired: Optional (Free General Queue; Paid Sugam Darshan ₹300; Mangala Aarti ₹500)
temples.majorFestivals: Maha Shivaratri (continuous 36-hour darshan), Dev Deepawali, Rangbhari Ekadashi, Shravan Maas

temples.name: Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Mandir
temples.nameLocal: श्री राम जन्मभूमि मंदिर अयोध्या धाम
alternativeNames: Ayodhya Ram Mandir; Ram Lalla Mandir
temples.description: The sacred birthplace of Lord Rama on the banks of the holy Sarayu River in Ayodhya. The newly constructed grand Nagara-style temple is built using pink Bansi Paharpur sandstone from Rajasthan across a 70-acre complex, designed by the Sompura family of master temple architects without the use of structural steel or iron.
temples.mainDeity: Bhagwan Shri Ram Lalla Virajman (5-year-old child form in black Shaligram stone)
temples.templeType: Grand Classical Nagara Stone Temple / Historic Avatara Kshetram
temples.establishedYear: Ancient traditional origin; monumental stone temple consecrated 2024 CE
temples.address: Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Path, Ayodhya, Uttar Pradesh
temples.source: Shri Ram Janmbhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust Portal
temples.ticketRequired: Free Entry (No ticket required for general darshan; Aarti passes online free)
temples.majorFestivals: Sri Rama Navami, Ayodhya Deepotsav (Diwali - Guinness record 2.2 million diyas on Sarayu), Vivaha Panchami

temples.name: Shri Krishna Janmasthan Temple Complex
temples.nameLocal: श्री कृष्ण जन्मस्थान मंदिर परिसर मथुरा
alternativeNames: Mathura Krishna Janmabhoomi; Keshavdev Temple; Katra Keshavdev
temples.description: The sacred prison cell (Kamsa's Karagar) where Lord Krishna appeared at midnight on Ashtami Rohini in Dwapara Yuga. The complex houses the underground stone Garbha Griha shrine, the magnificent Keshavdev temple, Bhagavata Bhavan, and the ancient Potra Kund holy water tank.
temples.mainDeity: Lord Krishna (Garbha Griha prison cell shrine of Vasudeva and Devaki)
temples.templeType: Historic Avatara Kshetram / Sapta Puri Site
temples.establishedYear: Ancient origin; present temple complex built 1953–1982 CE
temples.address: Deeg Gate, Mathura, Uttar Pradesh
temples.source: Shri Krishna Janmasthan Seva Sansthan Directory
temples.majorFestivals: Krishna Janmashtami (Midnight Mahapuja), Braj Ki Lathmar Holi, Radhashtami, Sharad Purnima

temples.name: Shri Kedarnath Jyotirlinga Temple
alternativeNames: Kedarnath Dham; Highest Jyotirlinga; Northern Himalayan Dham
temples.description: Standing majestically at an altitude of 3,583 metres (11,755 feet) amidst snow-clad peaks of the Garhwal Himalayas near the Chorabari glacier, origin of the Mandakini River. Constructed out of massive grey granite slabs without mortar, the temple miraculously withstood the catastrophic 2013 flash floods protected by the colossal 'Bhim Shila' boulder.
temples.mainDeity: Lord Shiva (Sadashiva in triangular natural rock humped bull form)
temples.templeType: Jyotirlinga (Highest - 3,583 m) / Chota Char Dham / Panch Kedar (#1)
temples.architecture: Katyuri / Classical Himalayan Ashlar Stone Architecture
temples.address: Kedarnath, Rudraprayag District, Uttarakhand
temples.source: Shri Badrinath-Kedarnath Temple Committee Official Gazette
temples.ticketRequired: Free Entry (Mandatory Uttarakhand Char Dham Registration biometric slip)
temples.majorFestivals: Kapat Opening (Akshaya Tritiya / May), Kapat Closing (Bhai Dooj / November), Badri-Kedar Utsav

temples.name: Shri Badrinath Temple (Badri Vishal)
alternativeNames: Badrinath Dham; Char Dham Badrinath; Badrikashram
temples.description: One of the holy Char Dham sites, located in the Garhwal hills on the banks of Alaknanda River at an elevation of 3,133 metres (10,279 ft). The 1-metre tall self-manifested black Shaligram deity of Lord Vishnu sitting in meditative Padmasana posture was retrieved from the Narad Kund and consecrated by Adi Shankaracharya in the 8th century CE.
temples.mainDeity: Lord Badri Vishal (Maha Vishnu in Padmasana meditative posture under Badri tree)
deities: Garuda, Kubera, Narada, Uddhava, Nara and Narayana
temples.templeType: Supreme Char Dham Pilgrimage Site / 108 Divya Desams (#106)
temples.architecture: Himalayan Pagoda Style with Colourful Wooden Facade
temples.establishedYear: 8th Century CE (Adi Shankara); stone shrine expanded by Garhwal Kings in 16th c. CE
temples.address: Badrinath, Chamoli District, Uttarakhand
temples.ticketRequired: Free Entry (Mandatory Char Dham biometric registration slip)
temples.majorFestivals: Kapat Opening (April/May on Akshaya Tritiya), Badri-Kedar Utsav (June), Kapat Closing (November on Diwali)

temples.name: Maa Jwala Ji Temple
temples.nameLocal: माँ ज्वाला जी मंदिर कांगड़ा हिमाचल प्रदेश
alternativeNames: Jwalamukhi Temple; Eternal Flame Shakti Peeth
temples.description: One of the 51 Shakti Peethas where the tongue of Goddess Sati fell. There is no idol; instead, nine natural perpetual blue flames burning without fuel through rock crevices in the sanctum have burned uninterrupted for centuries. Celebrated for Mughal Emperor Akbar offering a golden parasol (Chhatra) in humility after failing to extinguish the holy flame.
temples.mainDeity: Goddess Jwalamukhi (Nine perpetual natural blue flames emanating from natural rock fissures)
deities: Nine Flames (Mahakali, Annapurna, Chandi, Hinglaj, Vindhyavasini, Mahalakshmi, Saraswati, Ambika, Anjana)
temples.templeType: Maha Shakti Peeth (Tongue of Goddess Sati) / No Idol Shrine
temples.architecture: Indo-Sikh & Nagara Fusion with Gilded Dome
temples.address: Jwalamukhi, Kangra District, Himachal Pradesh
temples.majorFestivals: Chaitra Navratri & Ashwin Navratri (Lakhs of pilgrims climb to the shrine), Sawan Mela

temples.name: Sri Harmandir Sahib (The Golden Temple)
alternativeNames: Golden Temple Amritsar; Sri Darbar Sahib; Suvarna Mandir
temples.description: Surrounded by the holy Amrit Sarovar (Pool of Nectar), Sri Harmandir Sahib was founded by Guru Ram Das Ji and designed by Guru Arjan Dev Ji with four doors opening to the cardinal directions, demonstrating that people of all castes, creeds, and backgrounds are welcomed equally. Clad in 500 kilograms of pure gold foil by Maharaja Ranjit Singh.
temples.mainDeity: Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji (The Living Eternal Guru & Word of the Divine)
deities: Akal Takht Sahib (Seat of Temporal Authority), Dukh Bhanjani Beri, Baba Deep Singh Shaheed Sthan
temples.templeType: Supreme Spiritual Epicentre of Sikhism / Heritage Sacred Pool
temples.architecture: Sikh Architecture (Synthesis of Indo-Islamic and Hindu Rajput elements)
temples.address: Golden Temple Road, Amritsar, Punjab
temples.ticketRequired: Free Entry (No tickets; open to all humanity)
temples.majorFestivals: Baisakhi (Khalsa Sirjana Diwas), Prakash Purab Guru Nanak Dev Ji, Bandi Chhor Divas (Diwali Deepmala)

temples.name: Brahma Sarovar & Sthaneshwar Mahadev Temple
temples.nameLocal: ब्रह्म सरोवर एवं स्थानेश्वर महादेव मंदिर कुरुक्षेत्र
alternativeNames: Kurukshetra Holy Sarovar; Sthaneshwar Mahadev; Dharamkshetra
temples.description: Brahma Sarovar is an ancient colossal sacred water tank (1,800 m long by 1,400 m wide) mentioned in Mahabharata and Vamana Purana as the cradle of cosmic creation by Lord Brahma. Sthaneshwar Mahadev is the ancient temple where the Pandavas and Lord Krishna worshipped Lord Shiva and received his blessings for victory in the Mahabharata War.
deities: Sarveshwar Mahadev (located in the middle of Brahma Sarovar), Krishna (Geetopadesh)
temples.templeType: Ancient Cosmic Sacred Pool & Pandava Shiva Shrine
temples.architecture: Nagara with North Indian Step-Well Ghats
temples.establishedYear: Ancient Vedic origin; restored by Pushyabhuti Dynasty (Harsha) & Kurukshetra Development Board
temples.address: Thanesar, Kurukshetra District, Haryana
temples.majorFestivals: International Gita Mahotsav (December), Surya Grahan Mela, Somvati Amavasya

temples.name: Swaminarayan Akshardham Temple Delhi
temples.description: Guinness World Record holder as one of the world's largest comprehensive Hindu temple campuses (100 acres). Constructed entirely from Rajasthani pink sandstone and Italian Carrara marble without structural steel. Features 234 ornately carved pillars, 9 domes, 20,000 murtis, Gajendra Pith (elephant plinth with 148 stone elephants), and the Sahaj Anand water sound-and-light show.
temples.mainDeity: Bhagwan Swaminarayan (11-foot gilded bronze murti under the central dome)
deities: Gunatitanand Swami, Radha Krishna, Sita Rama, Lakshmi Narayana, Shiva Parvati
temples.templeType: Modern Monumental Stone Temple Complex / Spiritual Cultural Campus
temples.architecture: Classical Nagara & Pancharatra Shastra Stone Architecture
temples.address: NH 24, Pramukh Swami Maharaj Marg, New Delhi
temples.ticketRequired: Temple Entry Free; Exhibition & Water Show Ticketed (Exhibitions: ₹250 adults; Water show: ₹90)
temples.majorFestivals: Diwali & Annakut (over 1,000 vegetarian food offerings displayed), Janmashtami, Swaminarayan Jayanti

temples.name: Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Shrine
temples.nameLocal: श्री माता वैष्णो देवी श्राइन कटरा जम्मू कश्मीर
alternativeNames: Vaishno Devi Bhawan; Trikuta Hills Holy Cave; Mata Rani
temples.description: Located at an altitude of 5,200 feet in the fold of the three-peaked Trikuta Mountain. The Holy Cave houses no idols; devotees worship the sacred natural rock manifestations known as the Holy Pindies representing Maha Kali (destructive/protective force), Maha Lakshmi (wealth/prosperity), and Maha Saraswati (wisdom/learning), bathed continuously by icy natural spring waters.
temples.mainDeity: Maha Kali, Maha Lakshmi, Maha Saraswati (Three Natural Rock Pindies)
deities: Bhairavnath (on Bhairav Ghati peak 2 km above Bhavan)
temples.templeType: Sacred Holy Cave Shrine (Natural Pindies) / Maha Shakti Tirtha
temples.architecture: Natural Holy Cave with Modern High-Tech Pilgrim Terraces
temples.establishedYear: Ancient Cave; modernized platforms and tracks 1986–Present
temples.address: Bhavan, Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Shrine, Katra, Reasi District, Jammu and Kashmir
temples.source: Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Shrine Board Official Gazette
temples.ticketRequired: Free Entry (Mandatory RFID Yatra Access Card issued free at Katra Base)

temples.name: Shree Saibaba Sansthan Temple Shirdi
temples.nameLocal: श्री साईबाबा संस्थान मंदिर शिर्डी महाराष्ट्र
alternativeNames: Shirdi Sai Baba Temple; Samadhi Mandir Shirdi
temples.description: The holy samadhi shrine of the 19th-century saint Shree Sai Baba who taught 'Sabka Malik Ek' (One God Governs All) and 'Shraddha & Saburi' (Faith and Patience). The white Italian marble idol sits above his holy tomb in the grand Samadhi Mandir, adorned with a solid gold throne.

temples.name: Shree Trimbakeshwar Shiva Jyotirlinga Temple
temples.nameLocal: श्री त्र्यंबकेश्वर ज्योतिर्लिंग मंदिर नाशिक महाराष्ट्र
alternativeNames: Trimbak Temple; Tenth Jyotirlinga; Source of Godavari
temples.description: One of the twelve sacred Jyotirlingas, situated at the base of Brahmagiri Mountain where the sacred river Godavari originates. Unique because the Jyotirlinga inside the sanctum cavity features three thumbs-sized faces representing the holy trinity: Brahma, Vishnu, and Rudra, wearing a priceless gem-studded gold crown placed during Monday evening processions.
temples.mainDeity: Lord Trimbakeshwar (Unique three-faced Lingam representing Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva)

temples.name: Shree Siddhivinayak Ganapati Temple Prabhadevi
temples.nameLocal: श्री सिद्धिविनायक गणपती मंदिर प्रभादेवी मुंबई
temples.description: One of the richest and most frequently visited shrines in Mumbai. Consecrated in 1801 CE. The black stone deity features four arms holding a lotus, axe, modak, and prayer beads, flanked by Goddesses Riddhi and Siddhi. The gold-plated inner sanctum roof is adorned with 3.75 kg of pure gold.

temples.majorFestivals: Ganesh Chaturthi (10 days), Angaraki Sankashti Chaturthi, Maghi Ganesh Jayanti

temples.name: Shree Somnath Jyotirlinga Temple
temples.nameLocal: શ્રી સોમનાથ જ્યોતિર્લિંગ મંદિર પ્રભાસ પાટણ
alternativeNames: First Jyotirlinga; Somnath Patan; Shrine Eternal
temples.description: The foremost of the twelve sacred Jyotirlingas, perched on the windswept Arabian Sea shore where rivers Hiran, Kapila, and mythical Saraswati meet. Celebrated as the 'Shrine Eternal', rebuilt seven times across millennia following historical invasions. Reconstructed in pristine Kailash Mahameru Prasad style under Iron Man Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.
temples.mainDeity: Lord Shiva (Somnath - Lord of Soma / Moon God)
deities: Parvati Devi, Ganesha, Hanuman, Baan Stambh (Arrow Pillar)
temples.architecture: Maru-Gurjara (Chaulukya / Solanki Dynasty Revival by Sompura Sculptors)

temples.name: Shree Dwarkadhish Temple (Jagat Mandir)
alternativeNames: Dwarka Temple; King of Dwarka; Mokshapuri Dwarka; Char Dham
temples.description: One of the four supreme Char Dham sites and one of the seven Mokshadayani Puris. The majestic 5-storey Jagat Mandir is supported by 72 limestone pillars, crowned by a 78-metre spire that flies a colossal 52-yard flag (Dhwaja) depicting the sun and moon, visible from 10 km at sea and changed five times daily.
temples.mainDeity: Lord Krishna as Dwarkadhish (King of Dwarka in four-armed royal Trivikrama posture)
deities: Balram, Subhadra, Pradyumna, Aniruddha, Devaki, Satyabhama, Jambavati, Radhika
temples.templeType: Char Dham Pilgrimage Site / Sapta Puri / 108 Divya Desams
temples.address: Dwarkadhish Temple, Dwarka, Devbhumi Dwarka District, Gujarat
temples.majorFestivals: Janmashtami Mahotsav, Holi (Dolyatra), Sharad Purnima, Annakut Utsav

temples.name: Jagatpita Brahma Mandir Pushkar
alternativeNames: Pushkar Brahma Temple; Only Major Brahma Temple in India
temples.description: One of the very few surviving temples in the world dedicated to Lord Brahma, the Creator in the Hindu Trinity. Constructed with stone slabs and marble, topped with a distinctive red spire (Shikhara) and a goose (Hamsa) motif. The floor and inner walls are embedded with silver coins donated by devotees.
temples.mainDeity: Lord Brahma (Chaturmukha four-faced life-size deity in Padmasana)
deities: Goddess Gayatri, Savitri Devi (on Ratnagiri Hill above)
temples.templeType: Ancient Tirtharaj Shrine / Sole Prominent Brahma Temple
temples.address: Brahma Temple Road, Pushkar, Ajmer District, Rajasthan
temples.majorFestivals: Pushkar Camel Fair & Kartik Purnima Maha Mela (International festival)

temples.name: Shree Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga Temple Ujjain
temples.nameLocal: श्री महाकालेश्वर ज्योतिर्लिंग मंदिर उज्जैन मध्य प्रदेश
alternativeNames: Mahakal Ujjain; Dakshinavarti Jyotirlinga; Mahakal Lok
temples.description: One of the twelve sacred Jyotirlingas, revered as the sole Dakshinavarti (south-facing) Jyotirlinga, positioned at the prime meridian of ancient Indian astronomy. Renowned worldwide for the daily pre-dawn 'Bhasma Aarti' where the deity is worshipped with sacred cow-dung ash (vibhuti). The newly inaugurated 900-meter Mahakal Lok Corridor features 108 grand sculpted pillars depicting Lord Shiva's Anand Tandav.
temples.mainDeity: Lord Shiva as Mahakaleshwar (The Lord of Time and Death - facing South / Dakshinavarti)
deities: Omkareshwar (first floor), Nagchandreshwar (third floor, open only on Nag Panchami), Vriddha Mahakal
temples.templeType: Dakshinavarti Jyotirlinga (3rd) / Sapta Puri / Kumbh Mela Tirtha
temples.establishedYear: Ancient origin; present structure 1734 CE; Mahakal Lok 2022 CE

temples.majorFestivals: Maha Shivaratri (9-day Navratri of Shiva ending with Sehra Bandhan), Ujjain Simhastha Kumbh Mela (every 12 years), Shravan Sawari

temples.name: Maa Danteshwari Temple Dantewada
temples.nameLocal: माँ दंतेश्वरी शक्तिपीठ मंदिर दंतेवाड़ा छत्तीसगढ़
temples.description: One of the 51 sacred Shakti Peethas where the tooth (Daant) of Goddess Sati fell. Consecrated at the sacred holy confluence of Shankhini and Dankini rivers. Revered as the sovereign deity and Kuldevi of the royal family of Bastar and over 30 indigenous tribal communities who bring their local village deities (Angas and Chhatras) during Bastar Dussehra.
temples.mainDeity: Goddess Danteshwari (Six-armed black stone Mahishasuramardini holding sword, trident, discus, conch)

temples.name: Shree Mangueshi Temple Priol
temples.description: One of the largest, most famous, and prominent Hindu temples in Goa. Famous for its magnificent seven-storey octagonal Deepastambha (lamp tower) which illuminates the entire courtyard when lit with hundreds of oil lamps. Features a distinctive blend of Goan Hindu, Maratha, and Indo-Portuguese architectural styles with pristine blue and white domes.
temples.mainDeity: Lord Shiva as Manguesh (Incarnation born when Shiva playfully scared Parvati in tiger form)
deities: Parvati Devi, Ganesha, Mulkeshwar, Virabhadra, Saanteri

temples.name: Shree Jagannatha Temple Puri
alternativeNames: Puri Jagannath; Badadeula; Purushottama Kshetra; Srimandir
temples.description: One of the four sacred Char Dham pilgrimage centers of India. Built inside the towering 20-foot Meghanada Pacheri stone walls. The 214-foot Rekha Deula sanctum houses the Holy Trinity carved out of sacred Margosa (neem) wood, crowned by the eight-metal Nilachakra and Patitapabana flag. Famous for the sacred Mahaprasad (Chhappan Bhog) cooked in earthen pots over woodfire.

deities: Lord Balabhadra, Devi Subhadra, Sudarshana Chakra, Goddess Bimala, Mahalaxmi

temples.name: Konark Sun Temple (Surya Deula)
alternativeNames: Black Pagoda; Konark Sun Temple UNESCO World Heritage Site
temples.description: A monumental 13th-century architectural masterpiece conceived as a colossal chariot of the Sun God Surya, featuring 24 intricately carved stone wheels (3.7 metres in diameter) serving as precise sundials, pulled by seven galloping stone horses. Inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage list in 1984 as a pinnacle of Kalinga stone sculpture.

deities: Three chlorite stone images of Surya catching morning, noon, and sunset rays

temples.name: Dakshineswar Kali Temple
alternativeNames: Bhavatarini Temple; Dakshineswar Mandir; Sri Ramakrishna Sthalam
temples.description: Located on the eastern bank of the holy Hooghly (Ganga) River. Built by philanthropist Rani Rashmoni in 1855 CE. World-renowned as the spiritual seat where mystic saint Sri Ramakrishna Paramahamsa served as priest and achieved God-realization across all major world faiths. Features the grand three-storey Navaratna (nine-spire) temple, twelve identical Shiva temples along the riverbank, and the sacred Panchavati grove.

temples.name: Vishnupad Temple Gaya
alternativeNames: Gaya Dham; Footprint of Lord Vishnu; Pitru Tirtha Gaya
temples.description: Located on the bank of the holy Falgu River in Gaya. The sanctum enshrines the 40-centimetre footprint of Lord Vishnu stamped into solid basalt rock (Dharmasila), enclosed in an octagonal silver-plated basin. Lord Vishnu placed his holy foot on demon Gayasura who offered his body for cosmic sacrifice. World-famous for the Pitru Paksha Shraddha pilgrimage where millions offer Pinda Daan for the salvation of ancestors.

temples.name: Baba Baidyanath Jyotirlinga Temple Deoghar
temples.nameLocal: बाबा बैद्यनाथ ज्योतिर्लिंग मंदिर देवघर झारखंड
alternativeNames: Deoghar Baidyanath Dham; Ravana Jyotirlinga; Kamna Lingam
temples.description: One of the twelve sacred Jyotirlingas and also recognized as a Shakti Peeth (where the heart of Sati fell). Enclosed in a fortified courtyard containing 22 temples. Famously linked by the 'Gathbandhan' sacred red silk cloth connecting the spires of Baidyanath and Parvati temples. Epicentre of the historic 108-km barefoot Shravani Mela Kanwar Yatra from Sultanganj.

temples.name: Maa Kamakhya Devalaya Nilachal Hill
alternativeNames: Kamakhya Temple Guwahati; Yoni Peeth; Nilachal Mahapitha
temples.description: Perched atop the sacred Nilachal Hill overlooking the mighty Brahmaputra River. The supreme seat of Tantric Shaktism and the foremost of the 51 Shakti Peethas. The dark subterranean sanctum contains no sculpted idol; worship is offered to a natural fissure in the bedrock fed by an underground natural perennial spring. Features the unique Nilachal hybrid architectural style with a 16-sided beehive dome.

temples.name: Maa Tripura Sundari Temple (Matabari)
temples.nameLocal: মা ত্রিপুরা সুন্দরী মন্দির উদয়পুর ত্রিপুরা
alternativeNames: Matabari Temple; Kurma Peeth; 51 Shaktipeeth Udaipur
temples.description: One of the 51 sacred Shakti Peethas where the right foot of Goddess Sati fell. Constructed atop a hillock resembling the hump of a tortoise (Kurma Pristhakriti), hence celebrated as a Kurma Peeth. The holy temple pond, Kalyan Sagar, located right behind the temple, is home to sacred giant hillock turtles (Bostami / Black softshell turtles) and indigenous fishes protected by ancient royal edict.

temples.nameLocal: ஸ்ரீ வெற்றிமலை முருகன் திருக்கோயில் போர்ட் பிளேர்
alternativeNames: Port Blair Murugan Temple; Vetrimalai Kovil

festivals.Festival_Name: Srivari Annual Salakatla Brahmotsavam, Vaikunta Ekadasi, Rathasapthami, Ugadi Asthanam
festivals.Description: Garuda Vahanam witnesses over 500,000 devotees circumambulating the Four Mada Streets.

festivals.Festival_Name: Karthika Brahmotsavam, Panchami Theertham, Vasantotsavam, Navaratri
festivals.Description: Lakhs take holy dip in Padma Sarovaram as the divine Chakra Theertham is bathed.

festivals.Festival_Name: Maha Shivaratri Brahmotsavam (13 days), Giri Pradakshina, Nandi Seva
festivals.Description: Over 300,000 pilgrims participate in the Rathotsavam and midnight Lingodbhava Abhishekam.

festivals.Festival_Name: Maha Shivaratri Brahmotsavam (7 days), Ugadi Mahotsavam, Kumbhothsavam
festivals.Description: Paganalankarana (royal silk turban wrapping around the Vimana) witnessed by over 400,000 pilgrims.
festivals.Source: Sri Bhramaramba Mallikarjuna Swamy Devasthanam Gazette

festivals.Festival_Name: Dasara Navaratri (10 days), Shakambhari Utsavams, Bhavani Deeksha Viramana
festivals.Description: Over 1.5 million devotees gather during Dasara; grand Hamsa Vahana Teppotsavam on Krishna river.
festivals.Source: Sri Durga Malleswara Swamy Varla Devasthanam

festivals.Festival_Name: Annual Brahmotsavam (11 days), Narasimha Jayanthi, Vaikunta Ekadasi, Rathotsavam
festivals.Description: Tirukkalyanam and Divya Vimana Rathotsavam attended by over 300,000 devotees.
festivals.Source: Yadadri Temple Development Authority (YTDA) Official Gazette

festivals.Festival_Name: Sri Rama Navami (Kalyanotsavam), Vaikunta Ekadasi (Teppotsavam on Godavari)
festivals.Description: State festival attended by over 400,000 devotees; pearls sent on behalf of state governor.
festivals.Source: Sri Sita Ramachandra Swamy Devasthanam Register

festivals.Festival_Name: Maha Shivaratri (3-day fair), Ramappa Dance Festival (Kakatiya Heritage Festival)
festivals.Description: Classical dancers from across the world perform before the historic Madanika brackets.

festivals.Festival_Name: Chithirai Thiruvizha (1 month festival), Meenakshi Tirukkalyanam, Navaratri, Avani Moola Utsavam
festivals.Description: Over 1 million devotees witness the Celestial Wedding and Lord Kallazhagar entering Vaigai River.

festivals.Festival_Name: Maha Shivaratri (10 days), Thirukalyanam (Aadi Amavasai), Ramalinga Prathishta Utsavam
festivals.Description: Hundreds of thousands gather at Agni Theertham for ancestral rites and temple darshan.

festivals.Festival_Name: Sathaya Vizha (Birth anniversary of Raja Raja Chola I), Maha Shivaratri, Chithirai Brahmotsavam
festivals.Description: Grand state celebration featuring classical Bharatanatyam concerts with 1,000 dancers on the temple courtyard.

festivals.Festival_Name: Biennial Paryaya Mahotsava (every 2 years in January), Sri Krishna Janmashtami, Vittal Pindi, Laksha Deepotsava
festivals.Description: Ceremonial transfer of Akshaya Patra and administration to incoming pontiff; Car Street decorated with 100,000 oil lamps during Deepotsava.
festivals.Source: Sri Krishna Matha Paryaya Official Records

festivals.Festival_Name: Maha Shivaratri (grand seaside mela and Rathotsava), Karthika Deepotsava
festivals.Description: Massive chariot procession along the beach and night-long coastal bhajan sessions.

festivals.Festival_Name: Alpasi Utsavam, Painkuni Utsavam, Aaraattu (procession to Shangumugham Beach), Lakshadeepam
festivals.Description: Maharaja of Travancore leads the royal procession on foot with drawn sword to Shangumugham Beach.
festivals.Source: Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple Official Administrative Register

festivals.Festival_Name: Guruvayur Utsavam (10 days with Elephant Race / Anayottam), Chembai Music Festival, Guruvayur Ekadasi
festivals.Description: Anayottam (legendary elephant race) marks the start of the annual 10-day festival.
festivals.Source: Guruvayur Devaswom Managing Committee Official Register

festivals.Festival_Name: Vinayaka Chaturthi (24-day festival), Brahmotsavam, Sankatahara Chaturthi
festivals.Description: Massive procession of the Golden Chariot through the French and Tamil quarters of Puducherry.
festivals.Source: Government of Puducherry Hindu Religious Institutions Registry

festivals.Festival_Name: Maha Shivaratri (continuous 36-hour darshan), Dev Deepawali, Rangbhari Ekadashi, Shravan Maas
festivals.Description: All 84 ghats illuminated with over 1.5 million earthen lamps; lakhs throng the corridor.
festivals.Source: Shri Kashi Vishwanath Temple Trust Gazette

festivals.Festival_Name: Sri Rama Navami, Ayodhya Deepotsav (Diwali - Guinness record 2.2 million diyas on Sarayu), Vivaha Panchami
festivals.Description: Surya Tilak: Sunlight is optically focused precisely upon the forehead of Ram Lalla at 12:00 noon on Rama Navami.
festivals.Source: Shri Ram Janmbhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust Portal

festivals.Festival_Name: Krishna Janmashtami (Midnight Mahapuja), Braj Ki Lathmar Holi, Radhashtami, Sharad Purnima
festivals.Description: Over 1.2 million devotees gather as the Lord is bathed in pure milk, curd, honey, and ghee at the stroke of midnight.
festivals.Source: Shri Krishna Janmasthan Seva Sansthan Directory

festivals.Festival_Name: Kapat Opening (Akshaya Tritiya / May), Kapat Closing (Bhai Dooj / November), Badri-Kedar Utsav
festivals.Month: May to November (Temple closed during winters; deity shifts to Omkareshwar Temple Ukhimath)
festivals.Date: Akshaya Tritiya to Kartik Bhai Dooj
festivals.Description: Ceremonial procession of the Doli carrying the Utsava Murti to Ukhimath for 6 months of winter worship.
festivals.Source: Shri Badrinath-Kedarnath Temple Committee Official Gazette

festivals.Festival_Name: Kapat Opening (April/May on Akshaya Tritiya), Badri-Kedar Utsav (June), Kapat Closing (November on Diwali)
festivals.Month: May to November (Closed during winter; deity moves to Narsingh Temple Joshimath)
festivals.Description: The Akhand Jyoti lamp lit inside the sanctum continues burning miraculously throughout the 6 months of winter closure.

festivals.Festival_Name: Chaitra Navratri & Ashwin Navratri (Lakhs of pilgrims climb to the shrine), Sawan Mela
festivals.Description: Massive fairs with non-stop community kitchens (Langar) across the town.

festivals.Festival_Name: Baisakhi (Khalsa Sirjana Diwas), Prakash Purab Guru Nanak Dev Ji, Bandi Chhor Divas (Diwali Deepmala)
festivals.Description: Spectacular illumination of the Sarovar with hundreds of thousands of earthen lamps and green eco-fireworks.

festivals.Festival_Name: International Gita Mahotsav (December), Surya Grahan Mela, Somvati Amavasya
festivals.Month: November / December (Margashirsha Shukla Ekadasi - Gita Jayanti)
festivals.Description: Over 2 million visitors assemble for Gita recitation and spectacular floating lamps (Deepdan) across the water.

festivals.Festival_Name: Diwali & Annakut (over 1,000 vegetarian food offerings displayed), Janmashtami, Swaminarayan Jayanti
festivals.Description: Colossal illumination of the entire 100-acre campus with lakhs of lamps and spectacular water choreography.

festivals.Festival_Name: Chaitra Navratri & Sharad Navratri (Massive decoration with exotic flowers and dry fruits)
festivals.Description: Over 400,000 pilgrims trek during the 9-day festival; telecast live across global networks.
festivals.Source: Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Shrine Board Official Gazette

festivals.Festival_Name: Ramnavami Utsav (3 days), Guru Purnima Utsav, Vijayadashami (Sai Punyatithi Festival)
festivals.Date: Chaitra Shukla Navami, Ashadha Purnima, Ashwina Dashami
festivals.Description: Continuous 24-hour temple opening; over 300,000 pilgrims participate in Palki processions from Mumbai and Pune.
festivals.Source: Shree Saibaba Sansthan Trust Act (Govt of Maharashtra Gazette)

festivals.Festival_Name: Nashik-Trimbakeshwar Simhastha Kumbh Mela (every 12 years), Maha Shivaratri, Tripurari Purnima, Rathotsava
festivals.Month: February / March (Shivaratri) & Kumbh year (Jupiter in Leo)
festivals.Description: Millions of sadhus from Akhadas take holy royal bath (Shahi Snan) at Kushavarta Kund during Kumbh.
festivals.Source: Shri Trimbakeshwar Devasthan Trust Official Gazette

festivals.Festival_Name: Ganesh Chaturthi (10 days), Angaraki Sankashti Chaturthi, Maghi Ganesh Jayanti
festivals.Date: Bhadrapada Shukla Chaturthi to Anant Chaturdashi
festivals.Description: Over 200,000 devotees visit every Tuesday; over 1 million during the 10-day Ganeshotsav.
festivals.Source: Shree Siddhi Vinayak Ganpati Temple Trust Act, 1980

festivals.Festival_Name: Maha Shivaratri (5-day grand festival), Kartik Purnima Somnath Fair, Shravan Maas
festivals.Description: Continuous 42-hour temple opening on Shivaratri; over 500,000 pilgrims attend the coastal fair.
festivals.Source: Shree Somnath Trust Act & Official Gazette

festivals.Festival_Name: Janmashtami Mahotsav, Holi (Dolyatra), Sharad Purnima, Annakut Utsav
festivals.Description: Midnight Kanha Janmotsav attended by over 500,000 devotees dancing with Garba and bhajans.

festivals.Festival_Name: Pushkar Camel Fair & Kartik Purnima Maha Mela (International festival)
festivals.Date: Kartik Shukla Ekadasi to Kartik Purnima
festivals.Description: Attracts over 400,000 tourists and pilgrims worldwide; mass holy dip in Pushkar Lake.

festivals.Festival_Name: Maha Shivaratri (9-day Navratri of Shiva ending with Sehra Bandhan), Ujjain Simhastha Kumbh Mela (every 12 years), Shravan Sawari
festivals.Description: Sehra Bandhan on Shivaratri morning; the deity wears a massive floral crown and Bhasma Aarti takes place at noon instead of dawn.
festivals.Source: Shree Mahakaleshwar Temple Management Committee Gazette

festivals.Festival_Name: Bastar Dussehra (75-day festival), Chaitra & Shardiya Navratri, Fagun Mela (10 days)
festivals.Description: Scores of tribal village shamans assemble carrying local deities on wooden litters to pay homage to Maa Danteshwari.

festivals.Festival_Name: Magha Purnima Jatrotsav (grand annual car festival), Maha Shivaratri, Navaratri
festivals.Description: The deity is taken out in a monumental silver Ratha (chariot) pulled by thousands of devotees.

festivals.Festival_Name: Shree Gundicha Ratha Yatra (Car Festival - 9 days), Snana Yatra, Chandan Yatra (42 days), Bahuda Yatra, Suna Besha
festivals.Description: The Holy Trinity travels 3 km down Bada Danda on massive wooden chariots Nandighosha, Taladhwaja, and Darpadalana; over 1.5 million assemble.
festivals.Source: Shree Jagannatha Temple Act, 1955 (Odisha Act 11 of 1955)

festivals.Festival_Name: Konark Dance Festival (December 1-5 annually against the illuminated temple backdrop), Magha Saptami Chandrabhaga Mela
festivals.Description: World-class classical Odissi, Bharatanatyam, Kathak, and Kuchipudi troupes perform on the open-air stage.

festivals.Festival_Name: Shyama Puja (Deepawali Kali Puja), Kalpataru Utsav (Jan 1), Snana Yatra, Annakut
festivals.Description: Over 500,000 devotees walk across the skywalk on Kalpataru Day when Ramakrishna fulfilled every prayer.
festivals.Source: Dakshineswar Kali Temple Debottar Estate Official Records

festivals.Festival_Name: Pitru Paksha Mela (16 days in Bhadrapada/Ashwina), Chhath Puja, Rama Navami
festivals.Date: Bhadrapada Purnima to Sarva Pitru Amavasya
festivals.Description: Over 2 million pilgrims visit Gaya from across India and the diaspora to offer Pinda Daan rituals at Brahma Kund, Falgu Ghat, and Vishnupad.
festivals.Source: Bihar State Religious Trust Board Register

festivals.Festival_Name: Shravani Mela (month-long monsoon Kanwar festival), Maha Shivaratri, Basant Panchami
festivals.Date: Full month of Shravan (Ashadha Purnima to Shravana Purnima)
festivals.Description: Over 6 million saffron-clad pilgrims (Kanwariyas) walk 108 km barefoot carrying Ganga water from Sultanganj in pots balanced on bamboo poles.
festivals.Source: Baba Baidyanath Dham Temple Management Act & Gazette

festivals.Festival_Name: Ambubachi Mela (Monsoon in June - 4 days), Durga Puja (Navaratri with buffalo sacrifice traditions), Manasa Puja
festivals.Description: Sanctum doors remain shut for 3 full days commemorating the annual menstrual cycle of the Earth Goddess; reopened on 4th day with distribution of sacred red cloth (Angodak/Raktavastra).
festivals.Source: Maa Kamakhya Devalaya Bordeuri Samaj Official Gazette

festivals.Festival_Name: Diwali Matabari Mela (2-day state festival with lakhs of pilgrims), Navaratri
festivals.Description: Over 300,000 pilgrims congregate around Kalyan Sagar lake to light lamps and seek blessings.
festivals.Source: Maa Tripura Sundari Temple Trust Official Gazette

festivals.Festival_Name: Panguni Uthiram (Grand Chariot Festival), Thaipusam (Kavadi procession), Skanda Sashti
festivals.Description: Lakhs of island residents participate in the pulling of the golden chariot through the streets of Port Blair.
festivals.Source: Directorate of Tourism, Andaman & Nicobar Administration Directory

festivals.Festival_Name: Chaitra Navaratri; Sharad Navaratri; Maha Shivaratri
festivals.Description: Grand nine-day celebration with massive regional gatherings.

festivals.Festival_Name: Maha Shivaratri; Shravan Maas Somwar; Kartik Purnima
festivals.State: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
festivals.Description: All-night vigil and coastal prayers during Maha Shivaratri.
festivals.Source: Daman and Diu Tourism Department & District Administration

festivals.Festival_Name: Krishna Janmashtami; Diwali; Holi; Ram Navami
festivals.Description: Grand Janmashtami celebration with community feast and cultural programs.

festivals.Festival_Name: Kali Puja; Durga Puja; Saraswati Puja; Shivaratri
festivals.Description: Largest Hindu gathering in Mizoram during Diwali and Durga Puja.
Celebrated with island-wide interfaith harmony and coastal defense prayers.
